name: Olympus Mons
description: The largest volcano and highest mountain in the Solar System, a shield volcano rising ~22 km above the surrounding plains with a caldera ~80 km wide. Located on the Tharsis bulge.

name: Ascraeus Mons
description: The northernmost and tallest of the three Tharsis Montes shield volcanoes, rising ~18 km with a complex summit caldera and long lava flows.

name: Pavonis Mons
description: The middle shield volcano of the Tharsis Montes chain, rising ~14 km above mean surface level with a large summit caldera.

name: Arsia Mons
description: The southernmost of the Tharsis Montes shield volcanoes, rising ~17.7 km; its summit caldera is the largest of the three aligned volcanoes.

name: Alba Mons
description: A vast low-profile shield volcano north of the Tharsis Montes with the largest footprint of any volcano on Mars, though only ~6.8 km in relief.

name: Elysium Mons
description: The largest volcano in the Elysium volcanic province, rising ~14 km with a ~14 km wide caldera; the second major volcanic center after Tharsis.

name: Valles Marineris
description: A vast system of tectonic canyons stretching over 4,000 km along the Martian equator, up to 7 km deep; the largest canyon in the Solar System.

name: Noctis Labyrinthus
description: A network of intersecting graben and troughs at the western end of Valles Marineris on the Tharsis bulge, often called Mars's 'labyrinth of night'.

name: Hellas Planitia
description: A huge, roughly circular impact basin in the southern hemisphere, ~2,300 km across and over 7 km deep; one of the largest impact craters in the Solar System.

name: Argyre Planitia
description: A major impact basin ~800 km across in the southern highlands, formed ~3.9 billion years ago and once possibly holding an ancient lake.

name: Gale Crater
description: A 154 km diameter impact crater hosting Aeolis Mons (Mount Sharp), explored by NASA's Curiosity rover to assess ancient habitability.

name: Jezero Crater
description: A ~45 km crater on the western edge of Isidis Planitia containing a fossil river delta; the landing site of NASA's Perseverance rover.

name: Gusev Crater
description: A ~166 km crater that once held a lake fed by Ma'adim Vallis; landing site of NASA's Spirit rover.

name: Endeavour Crater
description: A ~22 km Noachian-aged crater in Meridiani Planum whose rim contains phyllosilicates; explored by NASA's Opportunity rover.

name: Victoria Crater
description: A ~750 m diameter impact crater in Meridiani Planum visited and imaged by NASA's Opportunity rover.

name: Utopia Planitia
description: A large lowland plain in the northern hemisphere and the Viking 2 lander site; IGG CAS studies report mineralogical evidence of water activity here.

name: Acidalia Planitia
description: A plain in the northern lowlands between Tharsis and Arabia Terra, containing the famous Cydonia region and the Viking 1 landing area nearby.

name: Medusae Fossae Formation
description: An extensive, enigmatic wind-scoured deposit straddling the equator between Tharsis and Elysium, possibly of volcanic ash origin.

name: Mareotis Fossae
description: A group of troughs (fossae) ~1,860 km long in the Arcadia quadrangle of the northern hemisphere, named after a classical albedo feature.

name: Kasei Valles
description: One of the largest outflow channel systems on Mars, ~1,780 km long, carved by ancient catastrophic floods north of Valles Marineris.

name: Ares Vallis
description: A major outflow channel ~1,700 km long leading from Argyre into Chryse Planitia; the Mars Pathfinder landing site lies near its mouth.

name: Ma'adim Vallis
description: A ~700 km long outflow channel draining south highland lakes northward into Gusev crater, over 20 km wide and 2 km deep in places.

name: Naktong Vallis
description: An ancient river valley ~494 km long in the Arabia quadrangle, named after a river in Korea, carved by past flowing water.

name: Shalbatana Vallis
description: An ancient outflow channel over 1,300 km long in Xanthe Terra, the westernmost of the southern Chryse outflow channels, imaged in detail by ESA's HRSC.

name: Meridiani Planum
description: An equatorial plain rich in hematite and layered sedimentary rocks; landing site of NASA's Opportunity rover, defining Mars's prime meridian region.

name: Arabia Terra
description: A vast, densely cratered upland region of Noachian terrain spanning ~4,500 km, marking the boundary between northern lowlands and southern highlands.

name: Terra Cimmeria
description: A heavily cratered southern-highland region ~5,400 km across noted for strong crustal remanent magnetization, evidence of an ancient Martian dynamo.

name: Xanthe Terra
description: A rugged highland region between Lunae Planum and Chryse Planitia that hosts many of the southern Chryse outflow channels, flown over by Mars Express.

name: North Polar Ice Cap (Planum Boreum)
description: A permanent dome of water ice with seasonal carbon dioxide frost atop layered polar deposits, imaged in detail by ESA's Mars Express and NASA missions.

name: South Polar Ice Cap (Planum Australe)
description: The southern residual polar cap, dominated by carbon dioxide ice over water-ice layered deposits, which grows and shrinks dramatically with the seasons.
